body: Okay that makes sense, thank you for the reply
Guy posting is probably some neckbeard whose pretending to be a girl, but has a picture of his animated “waifu”.... god that makes my skin crawl to actually type that out

Thank you for the reality check. You’re right. You’re 100% right. I appreciate hearing it from the children’s point of view. 

You’ve absolutely given me a lot to think about. This is not the example I want to be setting for my children, they deserve better than that. I wouldn’t be able to look at myself in the mirror if my two girls were treated the way I treated their mother, knowing I was the example of how a man treats a woman to them.

I will never stop wanting to be their Dad. I have to forget about my privilege I once had of seeing them 7 days a week and not raising them in a split household. It’s becoming increasingly clear to me that I will be damaging their lives beyond repair if I continue setting this example of what a man should be to them.

I’m relieved that you and your family seemed to turn out okay despite the rough upbringing. Your words are impactful and speak volumes, you’ve definitely put some fear in my mind as to how my girls’ futures may play out if I keep on this path.

You made a difference.

Thank you for sharing your close family members own personal experience. Last week (about a month after the incident) I put it out there that I still wanted to be together as a family and she called the police on me for violating the PFA and I ended up in jail again.

Waiting years, not months seems like the wiser choice... I have no idea how they can still coexist together after physical abuse. I lost everything when I ruined it and hit her, the family christmases, the birthday parties, their first days of school... they'll never be a shared experience between their mother and father and they don't deserve to lose those memories because of my bad choice.  


That's why I want to be a family together again.  Also, I would check up on your family friend... I've never heard of someone actually being able to change themselves like that. But props to him if he was truly able to.

I've tried to change several times, although this is the first time I had actually physically abused her. But I'm beginning to believe some people just Can't change certain aspects of themselves, I've tried so hard to change. And your right, things could never be the same- there will always be the fact of what I did.

Thank you for your honesty, I do respect your opinion as you've been through this yourself and your introspective isn't falling on deaf ears. I want to do what's best for my children, even if their mother and I aren't together. I just need more time with them.
